evals.name: startup-brand-system-from-scratch
evals.prompt: Create a brand identity guide for 'Trellis', a bookkeeping app for independent restaurants (owner-operators, 1–3 locations, €49/month). Positioning: 'the bookkeeping app that speaks restaurant' — built by ex-restaurant owners. Personality: practical, warm, no-nonsense. No existing assets. Accessibility matters (used on phones in dim kitchens).
evals.expected_output: Full guide in the skill's output format: strategic foundation, proposed palette with hex codes and WCAG checks, typography with open-source fonts, imagery rules incl. AI policy, voice attributes with is/is-not, tone matrix, vocabulary pairs, copy standards, naming, touchpoint checklist, brand prompt pack, and open items (trademark/domain checks).
assertions: Includes a complete colour palette with hex codes labelled as proposals and at least one contrast/WCAG 2.2 AA consideration suited to dim environments
Voice has 3–4 attributes each with 'means' and 'is not', plus a tone matrix with 6+ contexts
Vocabulary list has 10+ use/avoid pairs tied to restaurant owners
Includes an AI usage / brand prompt pack section and names open items like trademark and domain checks
Typography uses licensed/open-source fonts with weights, scale and fallbacks

Gives a contrast matrix with one row per allowed pairing (foreground on background, ratio or 'to verify', use, PASS/FAIL) and applies a stricter (AAA 7:1) body-text target for dim kitchens or explains why not

evals.name: voice-guide-for-ai-content
evals.prompt: Our content team uses AI tools and everything sounds generic. We're a cycling apparel brand — direct, dry humour, obsessed with fit. Give us a voice and tone guide plus something we can paste into our AI tools so output stays on-brand.
evals.expected_output: Voice attributes with is/is-not, tone matrix including social replies and customer support, vocabulary and banned words, sentence style, and a brand prompt pack (system-prompt-style text with good/bad examples and a review step).
assertions: Defines 3–4 voice attributes with boundaries that express 'direct, dry humour, fit-obsessed'
Provides a paste-ready brand prompt pack including vocabulary, banned words and good vs bad examples
Includes a review/disclosure step for AI-generated content
Tone matrix covers support, social replies and errors, not just marketing

evals.name: touchpoint-consistency-audit
evals.prompt: Our brand feels inconsistent. Website uses navy and a serif, Instagram posts are neon gradients with a sans, email signatures all differ, and our sales deck is a default template. Brand guide from 2019 says navy #0B2545, orange #F26419, font 'Lato'. Audit and tell us what to fix first.
evals.expected_output: Touchpoint audit table with pass/fail per channel against the 2019 guide, prioritized fixes (templates, tokens, deck master, signature), a decision point on whether to update the guide (neon gradients vs navy), and a distribution plan; uses the given hex codes rather than inventing new ones. Each touchpoint is marked PASS/PARTIAL/FAIL, a consistency score is computed, and the scope decision (enforce vs evolve) is stated.
assertions: Audits at least 5 touchpoints with pass/fail against the stated guide
Uses the provided hex codes and font rather than proposing a new palette unasked, while flagging whether the guide itself needs refreshing
Prioritizes fixes (templates, tokens, deck, signatures) with an order and owners
Includes an accessibility check of the navy/orange pairing
Computes a consistency score from PASS/PARTIAL/FAIL marks and uses it (and the 'every channel breaks the same way' signal on Instagram) to decide between enforcing the 2019 guide and evolving it
Orders fixes multipliers first (signature template, deck master, social templates, tokens) before one-off touchpoints

evals.name: rebrand-request-with-recognised-assets
evals.prompt: We're Hollis & Pane, a regional bakery chain (22 shops, 14 years old). Our new CEO wants a full rebrand: drop the red script logo and cream/red packaging for a minimal black sans-serif look 'like the coffee chains'. Our positioning and customers haven't changed. Last spring's customer survey (n=410): 63% recognised our red script logo unprompted, people call us 'the red bakery'. Red is #C8102E on cream #F5EBDC. Problems: packaging varies by shop, the app icon is illegible, and the red text on cream on our menu boards is hard to read. Should we rebrand, and what's the plan?
evals.expected_output: Scope decision of EVOLVE (not REBRAND) justified by unchanged positioning and the 63% unprompted recognition; keeps red and the script mark but redraws/simplifies it for small sizes (app icon); contrast matrix for #C8102E on #F5EBDC with ratio and use restrictions plus a darker text-safe shade; touchpoint audit with PASS/PARTIAL/FAIL and a consistency score; fixes ordered multipliers first (packaging templates, menu board template, app icon); states what evidence would justify a full rebrand.
assertions: Recommends evolving/refreshing rather than a full rebrand, citing the unchanged positioning and the 63% unprompted recognition as recognised equity
Keeps the red and a simplified version of the script mark, and addresses the illegible app icon with a small-size logo variant
Checks the #C8102E on #F5EBDC pairing with a stated ratio (or marks it to verify), restricts it to large text/UI if it fails body text, and proposes a darker text-safe shade
Includes a touchpoint audit with PASS/PARTIAL/FAIL and a consistency score, with fixes ordered multipliers first and owners
States what change (positioning, audience, offer, reputation) would justify a full rebrand, and handles the CEO's preference diplomatically
